question: I asked to cancel 20 minutes after ordering, but warehouse processing had already started. Does the 30-minute rule guarantee cancellation? If the order system later confirms cancellation before payment capture, is the pending card entry handled as a refund or as an authorization release, and what is the normal bank timing?

searches.query: I asked to cancel 20 minutes after ordering, but warehouse processing had already started. Does the 30-minute rule guarantee cancellation? If the order system later confirms cancellation before payment capture, is the pending card entry handled as a refund or as an authorization release, and what is the normal bank timing?

chunks.text: Payment authorization holds  When an order is placed, the card provider may show a pending authorization. The store captures payment when the order is dispatched. A pending entry and a captured payment are different states; the pending line alone does not prove a completed charge. If an order is cancelled before capture, the store releases the authorization rather than issuing a refund for a captured payment.  The card provider typically removes a released authorization within three to seven business days. The exact display time depends on that provider. Support cannot turn this policy range into a promise that a particular bank will remove the hold tomorrow. If a customer reports both a pending entry and a completed entry, check the payment record before calling it a duplicate charge.  The order-change policy controls whether an order can still be cancelled. This article does not extend the 30-minute request window or reverse warehouse processing. It also does not contain actual transaction records, card details, or authorization identifiers.

Do not tell a customer their order has been cancelled until the order system confirms cancellation. A customer may receive an authorization release at a different time from the cancellation confirmation; the payment-holds policy explains that distinction.

Changing or cancelling an order  Customers can request cancellation or an address correction during the first 30 minutes after placing an order, provided warehouse processing has not started. Both conditions must hold. A request sent within 30 minutes can still be too late if processing has already begun. After that point, support cannot guarantee an edit and the customer may need to use the return process after delivery.  Adding products to an existing order is not supported. Place a new order for additional products. Two orders do not automatically share a shipping charge even when they go to the same address. If an address correction would move the shipment outside the product's eligible delivery area, support must check the product restrictions before accepting it.  This page describes the policy window. It does not show the warehouse status of any specific order. A confirmation email proves the order was accepted, not that it is still editable. Do not tell a customer their order has been cancelled until the order system confirms cancellation.

When refunds arrive  The returns team normally inspects an ordinary parcel within five business days after warehouse receipt. Once the return is approved, the store submits the refund within two business days. A bank-card provider may then take another three to five business days to show the credit. These stages happen in sequence. A carrier delivery notification is not the same event as a completed inspection.  For planning, the longest published path is five business days for inspection, two for submission, and five for the card provider: up to 12 business days after warehouse receipt. That is a policy estimate, not a live payment-status lookup. Weekends and published holidays do not count as business days. A missing component or a dispute over condition can require further review.  Gift recipients receiving store credit are sent that credit after approval. The three-to-five-day bank-card processing period does not apply to issuing store credit. This page does not identify whether a particular return has been received, approved, or refunded.

A return request is not itself a refund. Customers receive a receipt after the inspection is complete. Original outbound delivery charges are not refunded for a change of mind. The return-label policy explains who pays for sending an item back. Do not send an item to the warehouse without an approved return request.

Price adjustments after a purchase  If the store lowers the price of the identical model, size, and color within seven calendar days of an online purchase, the purchaser may request one price adjustment. The lower-priced item must be available to buy when the request is made. A price on another retailer's website does not qualify. A different color or size is not an identical item for this policy.  Final-sale outlet items, bundle promotions, gift-card purchases, and one-use personalized coupons are excluded. The adjustment returns the eligible price difference to the original payment method after approval. It does not change the original order date, extend the return window, or remove a product's shipping restrictions.  Support needs the original purchase record and the current matching listing to decide a live request. These policy documents contain the rule, not today's product prices or inventory. A customer asking for the exact difference on a particular order needs those live values.

This page does not identify whether a particular return has been received, approved, or refunded. For that, support needs the live return record. A screenshot of the original purchase receipt does not show the refund's current status.

Collecting an online order in a store  Store pickup has no delivery fee when the chosen store has the product available. Wait for the ready-for-collection message before travelling. An order confirmation is not a ready message. The store holds a ready order for five calendar days from the ready message. Contact the store if collection within that period is not possible; the published policy does not guarantee an extension.  Bring the collection reference and identification matching the collecting person registered on the order. A purchaser may nominate another adult in the order portal before collection. A forwarded email alone does not add that person to the collection record. Inspect large items at the store and ask staff for help with loading when needed.  Pickup eligibility and stock are specific to each store. The online product catalog does not establish which store has an item today. The published pickup process cannot answer a live stock question or reserve a product on its own. Product return and warranty windows start from the recorded collection date for a pickup order.

Exchanging a size or color  For a domestic order, an eligible unused product can be exchanged for a different size or color of the same model. The exchange keeps the original paid item price even if the current listing price changed. The replacement must be available when the request is approved. Exchanges into a different model are handled as a return followed by a new purchase at the new model's price.  The warehouse holds an approved replacement for seven calendar days. The customer must hand the returning parcel to the carrier within that period. The hold does not last until the parcel physically arrives at the warehouse. If the dispatch deadline passes, the reservation is released and availability must be checked again. Support cannot promise stock from a catalog description.  Exchanges use the same unused-condition and eligibility-window rules as standard returns. The store does not offer direct international exchanges. An international customer may use the return route if eligible and place a separate new order.

answer.answer: No, the 30-minute rule does not guarantee cancellation. A request sent within 30 minutes can still be too late if warehouse processing has already begun, and both conditions must hold [7a1120acbd6d8a9f]. If the order system confirms cancellation before payment capture, the store releases the authorization rather than issuing a refund for a captured payment [e6cc30b70c422489]. The card provider typically removes a released authorization within three to seven business days, though the exact display time depends on the provider [e6cc30b70c422489].
